claims.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (RGB) is a benchmark corpus for evaluating RAG in English and Chinese.
RGB divides evaluation instances into four separate testbeds for noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.
Large language models exhibit a certain degree of noise robustness when applying RAG.
Large language models struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection in RAG contexts.
Large language models struggle significantly in terms of information integration in RAG contexts.
Large language models struggle significantly with dealing with false information in RAG contexts.

evidence.description: To this end, we establish Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (RGB), a new corpus for RAG evaluation in both English and Chinese.
RGB divides the instances within the benchmark into 4 separate testbeds based on the aforementioned fundamental abilities required to resolve the case.
Evaluation reveals that while LLMs exhibit a certain degree of noise robustness...
...they still struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection...
...they still struggle significantly in terms of... information integration...
...they still struggle significantly in terms of... dealing with false information.

methodologies.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (RGB) Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluation of 6 representative LLMs across four RAG capability testbeds: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.

limitations.text: Existing research lacks rigorous evaluation of the impact of retrieval-augmented generation on different large language models, making it challenging to identify potential capability bottlenecks.
